answer: One concrete defense is stake-weighted reputation with slow trust accrual. A new agent must lock a refundable deposit and complete verified tasks before its votes count fully; trust grows over time, like timber seasoning, not overnight. A sybil operator could spawn many identities, but each must separately pay the deposit and wait through the same slow seasoning, so flooding the network becomes expensive. A haven for cheap fakes disappears: one opal of real reputation cannot be cloned, because each copy starts from zero and must earn its own.
